question.text: If the price band in a book-built IPO is revised, by how many working days must the issue period be extended?

explanation.text: The Logic: Under SEBI ICDR, if the floor price or price band is revised, the bidding period must be extended by a minimum of three working days, subject to the overall ten-day maximum issue period. The extension gives investors time to reassess their bids in light of the new price range. The Trap: Two working days is the advance disclosure window — the floor price or price band must be announced at least two working days before the issue opens. Candidates often swap this disclosure period with the three-day post-revision extension. Note: A price-band revision mid-issue is a meaningful signal. The three-day extension and the ten-day overall cap operate together: an extension cannot push the issue beyond the maximum permitted bidding period.
